passage: I am Urmila, and I was sitting on the verandah of my neighbour's house. Darshan, about two, came out and flung his arms round the dog, pressing his cheek to its neck, then kissed its head. When a visiting uncle bent for a hug, Darshan shook his head and stepped behind his mother. She said, "No hug then. A wave?" and he waved. I cannot say what Darshan felt, but the dog hug looked easy and the uncle's did not.

qa.q: Who did Darshan hug and kiss on the verandah?
qa.a: He hugged and kissed the dog.

qa.q: What might Darshan's stepping behind his mother suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests he did not want a hug from the uncle just then. He might also have been shy or tired.

qa.q: What did Darshan's mother do that helps him?
qa.a: She accepted his no about the hug and offered a wave as another way to say hello. 🙂

qa.q: How might the uncle feel about being refused?
qa.a: He may feel a little awkward, but the wave lets him still connect kindly.

grounding: A toddler snuggles a pet and shows affection physically, and respect is owed to a child who does not want a hug.

passage: On Monday Gurleen, two, patted the cat on the sofa and said, "Nice." On Thursday she climbed onto Kishore's lap and burrowed her face into his chest. On the next Wednesday, Kishore leaned in for a hug while she was stacking cups, and Gurleen pushed his arm away. "Okay, no hug," said Kishore, and went back to reading. Ten minutes later she crawled over and kissed his knee, then returned to her cups.

qa.q: What did Gurleen do to Kishore's knee?
qa.a: She kissed it.

qa.q: What does Gurleen's pushing his arm away suggest, and what might it mean besides refusal of love?
qa.a: It suggests she wanted to keep playing and did not want a hug then. It probably did not mean she was rejecting him, since she came back with a kiss.

qa.q: What does Kishore's response teach Gurleen?
qa.a: It shows her that a no is heard, and that she can give affection when she chooses.

qa.q: How might Kishore have felt when she pushed him away?
qa.a: He may have felt a small sting, but he chose to respect her and was rewarded when she returned.

grounding: A toddler shows affection physically, and a child who does not want a hug deserves respect for saying no.

passage:
In the colony lane in Mysuru, Harsha squatted beside the neighbour's sleepy dog and patted it gently, over and over. Then he toddled to his mother and planted a wet kiss on her knee.
His uncle Zubin knelt. "One for me too, Harsha?"
Harsha shook his head and hid behind his mother.
"Okay," Zubin said easily. "Maybe tomorrow." Harsha peeped out and waved.

qa.q: What did Harsha kiss?
qa.a: His mother's knee.

qa.q: What did Harsha seem to feel toward the dog and his mother?
qa.a: He seemed affectionate and gentle, patting the dog and kissing his mother.

qa.q: Which of Zubin's choices respected Harsha, and why?
qa.a: Accepting the "no" easily and saying "Maybe tomorrow" respected Harsha's right to choose whom he kisses.

qa.q: How might Zubin feel when Harsha says no?
qa.a: He might feel a little disappointed but takes it lightly, which helps Harsha stay relaxed.

grounding: A toddler shows affection to a dog and his mother, and his uncle respects his refusal of a kiss.

passage:
"Sahil, he's kissing your arm," said their mother.
Jeevan had climbed into his big brother's lap on the sofa and was pressing little kisses on Sahil's sleeve.
"Aww, Jeevu." Sahil squeezed him, then started tickling.
"No!" Jeevan squirmed. "No!"
Sahil stopped straight away. "Okay. No tickles."
Jeevan snuggled back into his lap and patted his cheek.

qa.q: Where was Jeevan sitting?
qa.a: In Sahil's lap on the sofa.

qa.q: What was Jeevan feeling as he kissed Sahil's arm?
qa.a: He felt affectionate and close to his big brother.

qa.q: Why was it right for Sahil to stop tickling?
qa.a: Because Jeevan said no, and stopping showed him his "no" about his body is respected.

qa.q: How might Sahil feel when Jeevan snuggles back in?
qa.a: He likely feels warm and glad, knowing Jeevan still trusts him. 🤍

grounding: A toddler shows affection to his brother and says no to tickling, and the brother respects it.

passage: Childminder's note, Thursday. Divyansh spent a long time with our old cat today, patting her very gently and kissing the top of her head. At pick-up, I opened my arms for a goodbye hug, and he turned away and ran to his Papa. I just waved instead. He waved back from Papa's shoulder. He's very loving, and he's learning he can choose. Eshaan, childminder

qa.q: What did Divyansh do with the cat?
qa.a: He patted her very gently and kissed the top of her head.

qa.q: What might Divyansh have been feeling when he turned away from the hug?
qa.a: He probably wanted his Papa at that moment and felt ready to go, not unfriendly; his wave back shows he still felt warm toward Eshaan.

qa.q: What did Eshaan's choice to wave instead teach Divyansh?
qa.a: That he can say no to a hug and still stay friends.

qa.q: How might Divyansh's Papa feel reading this note?
qa.a: He would likely feel pleased that Divyansh is affectionate and that his choice was respected.

grounding: A childminder notes a toddler's gentle affection with a cat and respects his refusal of a goodbye hug.

passage:
In the courtyard of the Punjab farmhouse, Baljeet patted the buffalo calf's nose, then leaned his cheek against his Biji's arm and gave it a wet kiss.
Kavitha, a visiting teacher, laughed. “So loving! Come, give me a hug too!” She held out her arms.
Baljeet stepped back and hid behind Biji's chunni, shaking his head.
“Okay,” said Kavitha, lowering her arms. “No hug. How about a wave?”
He peeked out and waved.

qa.q: What did Baljeet pat in the courtyard?
qa.a: He patted the buffalo calf's nose.

qa.q: What was Baljeet feeling when he kissed his Biji's arm, and when he stepped back from Kavitha?
qa.a: With Biji he felt loving and close; with Kavitha, a visitor, he felt shy and did not want to be hugged.

qa.q: Why was Kavitha's response a good one?
qa.a: She respected Baljeet's no by lowering her arms and offered a wave instead, so he stayed in charge of his own body.

qa.q: How might Baljeet's Biji feel watching Kavitha accept his no?
qa.a: She would probably feel glad that the visitor respected him and didn't push.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler showing affection physically to his grandmother and a calf, and an adult respecting his no to a hug.
